connection._radio_note: Channel and group are derived from the board's name per radio-robot-lib docs/design/radio-addressing.md (channel 11 + n % 73, group 15 + n % 241; adopted 2026-09-13). Change only to resolve a name collision.
connection._v6_radio_link_note: 2026-09-06: tigez has NO WiFi module (no wifi_ip), so the v6 radio link over the relay is its only untethered carrier. pxt-nezha-diffdrive's make_deploy.py reads this key (_read_robot_radio_link) and boots the radio link in test.ts; without it the build defaults to OFF and a tigez placed on the field is unreachable -- MEASURED that day: firmware 1.20260906.7 built without it answered nothing to HELLO/PING/ID/STATUS through the relay on 55/114 while the camera showed it live on the field.

vision._note: MEASURED tigez 2026-08-30 (9-pose circle solve rms 0.18 cm) and CORRECTED 2026-08-31: the tag plates are REMOVABLE (top = robot front, bottom = back) and the 08-30 solve measured a mounting that sat ~90 deg off; +91.15 was that mounting's value, not the tag's. With the plate on correctly, -89.65 makes aprilcam report robot heading (verified: yaw reads true heading +-1 deg; 180-deg pivot wobble 0.50 cm, fieldtour6 session). The ~-90 all fleet tags carry cancels aprilcam's yaw convention (tag x-axis / paper-right), not a physical rotation. aprilcam registrations are IN-MEMORY PER-SESSION by design -- re-register at every session start, then probe-fit the heading offset with a ~12 cm drive before the first real leg (pxt-nezha-diffdrive reports/tigez-field-square-20260831.md).
vision._units_note: tag_offset_x/y/z are MILLIMETRES, the tag relative to the CENTRE OF ROTATION in the robot frame (x forward, y left). tag_offset_yaw is DEGREES and is the FULL mount yaw: -90 (AprilCam's fixed front-edge-to-hat convention, see pxt-nezha-diffdrive .claude/rules/tag-yaw-is-the-front-edge-not-the-hat.md) plus the physical plate residual. Feed it to the daemon as mount_yaw_rad; do NOT add the 90 again in your own code. Nothing read tag_offset_yaw as of 2026-09-05, so this fixes the convention: it matches tigez's previous non-schema tag_mount_yaw_deg -89.65, which was -90 + 0.35 residual.
vision._provenance: TIGEZ-MEASURED 2026-09-05 by pxt-nezha-diffdrive tests/calibration/mount.py on the SECONDARY playfield (110x70, camera hd-usb-camera): 9 rest poses over 8 +-90 pivots, rms 1.1 mm, verification drift 0.06 cm/pivot -- the tightest solve of the session. firmware_bake._note: MEASURED tigez 2026-09-03 on the playfield, camera-truthed, tests/playfield/turn_calibration.py, reports/tigez-turn-cal-20260903/: baseline (slip 0.952, overrun 0) over-rotated a flat +4.4 deg per pivot at 60 mm/s and +2.7 at the default cruise (~185 mm/s); overrun 5.5 mm + slip 0.96 (b_eff 119.0 mm at the 114.2 firmware default) centred the default-cruise sweep: 36 pivots of +-90/107/180, per-angle mean +0.8/+1.6/0.0 deg (06-confirm). slip here is 0.96 x 114.4/114.2 so b_eff is unchanged with the caliper trackwidth baked. Residual is speed dependent (end-of-pivot overrun grows with cruise): at 60 mm/s these values under-rotate 90s by ~2 deg. travel_calib from the 2026-08-30 80 cm run.
firmware_bake._stop_distance_provenance: UNVERIFIED on the sprint-029 engine, set 2026-09-04 by pxt-nezha-diffdrive when tigez was reflashed onto it. The previous key here was pivot_overrun_mm 5.5 -- the PRE-029 engine's post-target coast, measured camera-truthed (see the notes above) and superseded: 029's predictive arrival removes that coast by design (docs/design/motion-profile-unification.md S6.3), and tovez measured stop_distance 0 on it (captures/bench-acceptance-029-20260904d, pivot-gates Phase A). Baking the old coast into the new engine would under-rotate by about that much. Re-measure per design S10.2: lag_s first (WHEELS_V step, TLM FULL), then 10 floor-cruise pivots by camera for stop_distance_mm. lag_s measured 2026-09-04 (see _lag_provenance).

calc_20260917._method: MEASURED 2026-09-17 by calc (Calibrate C, nezha-robot-template test/calibratec.ts) on the alternating iron cross, playfield 4 (arducam-ov9782-usb-camera). METHOD: an eight-sector cross of 45 deg radial wedges; the robot spins on the middle and every line-sensor transition is logged against odometry heading. One sensor's CONSECUTIVE crossings are 45 deg apart whatever its radius, lateral offset or lever arm, and the eight sectors sum to 360 so a centring error cancels over a whole revolution -- so unlike calt and the camera-pivot methods it needs neither a known lever nor a fixed centre of rotation, which these robots do not hold. A spin measures ONLY the effective track b = trackwidth/rotational_slip, never the two separately, so trackwidth stays the caliper measurement and the slip carries the scrub. Slip is stored to 3 decimals because setConfigValue stores round(value*1000) and no more survives. slip = 11.44/11.777 = 0.9714 -> 0.971.
calc_20260917._spin_rate: THE COMMANDED SPIN RATE IS NOT THE TRUE ONE. calc derives its wheel speed from its ANCHOR b (11.996 cm), so every robot spins its wheels at the same 73.3 mm/s, but the yaw rate that produces is 70 * b_anchor / b_true. On this robot that is 70 * 11.996/11.777 = 71.3 deg/s. Describe this result as 'commanded 70 deg/s, 73.3 mm/s per wheel', never as 'measured at 70 deg/s'.
calc_20260917._findings: THIS DOES NOT CONFIRM EITHER EARLIER NUMBER, IT SPLITS THEM. This file's previous slip 0.9617 on the 114.4 caliper implied b 118.96 mm; nezha-robot-template boot.ts's calt result implied 116.47 mm. Those two disagree by 2.1% and calc lands almost exactly halfway. calc is preferred on the estimator grounds above, not because it agreed with anything -- and those grounds bite hardest here: this robot's sensor bar is mounted ~7 deg skew and its 9 cm lever doubles calt's arcsin(d/r) sensitivity to a centring error relative to gopiv's 17 cm. CLEANEST PIVOT IN THE FLEET: per-channel gap sd 1.7-3.7 deg and only ~0.25 cm of walk per revolution, against gopiv's 7.0-7.6 / ~0.5 cm on the SAME cross. THE BREAKAWAY FLOOR WAS NEVER CHECKED ON THIS ROBOT. It was run at 70 on the strength of gopiv's sweep alone (see gopiv.json). The small walk is at least consistent with being above the floor, but the floor was not located here and there is reason to expect it to move: the fleet's three chassis load their casters very differently and caster loading is what the breakaway is about. Sweeping costs no reflash -- cttune sets the rate over the wire. CHASSIS: one caster on a short arm, well balanced with weight over the wheels, so it scrubs less than gopiv (Eric, 2026-09-17).
